text: Assumption: StopOffer() is typically called before destruction of the object by the destructor in order to cleanly terminate ongoing forwardings of the DM prior to object release — is this correct?
text_en: Assumption: StopOffer() is typically called before destruction of the object by the destructor in order to cleanly terminate ongoing forwardings of the DM prior to object release — is this correct?
norm: stopoffer is typically called before destruction of the object by the destructor in order to cleanly terminate ongoing forwardings of the dm prior to object release
assumption: StopOffer() is typically called before destruction of the object by the destructor in order to cleanly terminate ongoing forwardings of the DM prior to object release.
rationale: The destructor is declared as non-thread-safe and SWS_DM_00767 specifies deactivation, but does not define an automatic call in the destructor.

original.text: Annahme: Interpretation: StopOffer() dürfte typischerweise vor der Zerstörung des Objekts durch den Destruktor aufgerufen werden, um laufende Weiterleitungen des DM vor der Objektfreigabe sauber zu beenden — trifft das zu?
